PullRequest.Title: Add customization marketplace install telemetry
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

- add a shared `chatCustomizationMarketplace.install` event for both the unified Marketplace and legacy Available sections
- report only bounded `surface`, `customizationType`, `installKind`, and `outcome` values plus measured duration
- cover Marketplace skill, MCP, plugin, configured-plugin, and Copilot connector installs
- cover legacy Available-section MCP gallery and configured-plugin installs using the same schema for direct comparison
- make `chat.customizations.marketplace.enabled` experiment-controlled and log its standard `experimentTrigger` when the Customizations editor opens in both control and treatment arms
- avoid collecting marketplace identifiers, source IDs, search queries, repository paths, URLs, error messages, or customization content

## Testing

- Passed: `npm run transpile-client && ./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/common/customizationMarketplaceInstallTelemetry.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/aiCustomization/customizationMarketplaceInstallService.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/aiCustomization/mcpListWidget.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/aiCustomization/pluginListWidget.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/chatConfiguration.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/aiCustomization/aiCustomizationManagementEditor.test.ts` (360 passing)
- Passed: `npm run typecheck-client`
- Passed: `npm run valid-layers-check`
- Passed: `npm run hygiene`
- Passed: `npm run eslint -- src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/customizationMarketplaceInstallTelemetry.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/aiCustomization/customizationMarketplaceInstallService.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/aiCustomization/mcpListWidget.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/aiCustomization/pluginListWidget.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/aiCustomization/customizationMarketplaceConfiguration.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/aiCustomization/aiCustomizationManagementEditor.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/common/customizationMarketplaceInstallTelemetry.test.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/aiCustomization/customizationMarketplaceInstallService.test.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/chatConfiguration.test.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/aiCustomization/aiCustomizationManagementEditor.test.ts`
- Passed: `node build/azure-pipelines/common/extract-telemetry.ts`

Suggested manual verification: open Chat Customizations with Marketplace enabled and disabled, install an MCP server or plugin from the visible surface, and verify that `chatCustomizationMarketplace.install` differs only by `surface` while retaining the same bounded type, install-kind, outcome, and duration fields.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or reopen the Chat Customizations editor while the marketplace setting remains at its experiment-provided default
Scenarios.CriticalPath: setInput performs one configuration inspection, then calls the experiment-trigger helper before the existing editor-open telemetry and EditorPane.setInput. The helper's bounded registry lookup and local telemetry enqueue are synchronous; telemetry transport is not awaited and remains off the editor-open critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch the new experimentTrigger event through configured telemetry appenders; desktop/remote appenders can enqueue IPC and web appenders enqueue network telemetry, while the log appender can write the telemetry log.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one new event per window for this setting, regardless of editor reopen count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The editor already emitted chatCustomizationEditor.opened on each setInput, but did not emit this once-per-window experimentTrigger event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only bounded sanitization/appender enqueue occurs synchronously before editor setup continues; IPC/network completion is not awaited.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Editor-open frequency within one window. Configuration inspection remains constant-size across eight known layers, and the experiment event is deduplicated to one event per telemetry service/window and treatment name.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous editor setup; no queue, parallel work, or new concurrent boundary. WeakMap/Set state coalesces repeated opens to one experiment event.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The first eligible open creates the per-telemetry-service Set and records the treatment; subsequent warm opens still perform the constant-size configuration inspection and registry lookup but return before telemetry dispatch. Explicitly configured values skip the helper.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed call site, WeakMap/Set deduplication, and synchronous telemetry dispatch path were directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Appender implementations and enabled telemetry modes vary by product environment, but the new event's cardinality and bounded payload are established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Added work is constant-size and the only new boundary is deduplicated to one asynchronous telemetry event per window.

Scenarios.Scenario: Install a skill, MCP server, plugin, configured plugin, or Copilot connector from the unified customization marketplace
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing install operation still performs the same type-specific install and record reconciliation. The new wrapper starts one stopwatch and emits one bounded telemetry event after success or failure before the install promise settles; transport completion is not awaited.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Perform the existing type-specific install: marketplace/plugin fetches, MCP management installation, Git/package/plugin installation, skill installation, or connector connection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing install workflow per unique pending key; internal calls vary by installation kind but are unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same doInstall or connector operation and addRecord path ran before this PR with the same pending-key coalescing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These existing boundaries dominate install latency and must complete before success is shown.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist and reconcile the installation record after the install succeeds.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One record update per effective successful install.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Record creation, upsert, and reconciliation were already awaited.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before install completion, unchanged by the wrapper.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch chatCustomizationMarketplace.install with five bounded scalar fields.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one new event per effective success, error, or cancellation after pending-key coalescing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No shared install-outcome telemetry event was emitted for this operation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Bounded local sanitization and enqueue happen before the promise settles; transport is not awaited.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective cardinality is one operation per unique marketplace resource/connector key. Concurrent callers for the same key share the existing pending promise and therefore produce one event, not one per caller.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing pending-key coalescing remains intact. Different resource keys may install concurrently as before; the diff adds no fan-out, limiter bypass, or extra install task.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing source/manifest/plugin caches and warm behavior are unchanged. Configured-plugin fetches, manifest retrieval, and installation records follow their prior cache semantics; telemetry is one event per effective attempt with no retained per-resource cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: install ownership, pending-key coalescing, wrapper placement, and all type branches were directly inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact installation duration and transport implementation vary by customization kind and environment, but those expensive installation boundaries are pre-existing; the introduced payload is fixed-size.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The wrapper neither duplicates installation work nor increases boundary cardinality; one fixed-size telemetry event is negligible relative to the user-initiated install.

Scenarios.Scenario: Install an MCP server from the legacy Available section
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing MCP workbench install remains awaited, followed by the new bounded outcome event, then status and refresh. Telemetry transport itself is not awaited.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Install the selected server through mcpWorkbenchService and mcpManagementService.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing management install per click.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same mcpWorkbenchService.install call ran directly before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited and dominant on the install critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch one bounded available/mcpServer/mcpGallery outcome event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One new event per completed or failed attempt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No shared install-outcome event was emitted.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only local enqueue is synchronous before status/refresh; transport completion is off path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One event per user install attempt. The clicked row's button is disabled during the operation; independent rows can still be installed concurrently exactly as before.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No new concurrency or fan-out. The wrapper tracks the one existing promise; no additional MCP management call is created.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: MCP gallery/install cache behavior is unchanged. The telemetry wrapper has no cache or retained per-server state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed click handler and transitive workbench install implementation were directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The MCP management backend depends on platform and package type, but its call count is unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The PR adds no extra install boundary and only one fixed-size event per explicit user action.

Scenarios.Scenario: Install a plugin from the legacy Available section
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing plugin install, including trust checks and source-specific Git/package/local filesystem work, remains the sole install operation. The wrapper emits one bounded event before the handler updates the button and refreshes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Install the plugin from its source, potentially using Git, npm/pip, or local filesystem operations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing plugin install workflow per click.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The handler directly awaited the same installPlugin call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited and dominant before UI completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch one bounded available/plugin/configuredPlugin outcome event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One new event per completed or failed attempt, independent of plugin metadata size.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No shared install-outcome event was emitted.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only bounded local telemetry processing occurs synchronously; transport completion is not awaited.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One event per clicked plugin install attempt. Different plugin rows may be installed independently as before; payload size does not scale with plugin metadata because only bounded categories and duration are logged.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The row button prevents duplicate clicks on that row during the attempt. Cross-row concurrency is unchanged, and the diff creates no additional subprocess or install task.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Configured marketplace and installed-plugin state are consumed exactly as before. The telemetry wrapper does not retain plugin identifiers or add a cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the handler and source-specific install service were directly inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Source-specific install cost varies widely, but that work is unchanged and the introduced telemetry payload remains fixed.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. There is no increased subprocess/filesystem/network multiplicity, unbounded serialization, or retained state.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 10 changed files and all diff pages. Traced editor-open telemetry and all unified/legacy install paths through telemetry appenders and existing install boundaries. The PR introduces only fixed-size, once-per-window or once-per-effective-operation telemetry work; it does not add scaling boundary calls, defeat install coalescing, retain unbounded state, or move heavyweight work onto a hotter path.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
